forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: Executive report - Affordable housing acquisitions in Farnham 150926
findings.headline: Property acquisitions transferring to West Surrey Council on 1 April 2027 vesting date during local government reorganisation.
findings.detail: Major property acquisition proceeding before reorganisation vesting date when Waverley merges into West Surrey Council. Council confirms acquisition is necessary and proportionate for continued service delivery through transition. 48 homes and associated HRA borrowing will form part of housing stock and liabilities transferring to successor authority.
findings.matters: Large capital asset acquisition and revenue-generating operations integration during major local government reorganisation presents execution and transition risk; successor council inherits both assets and borrowing obligations.
findings.quote: the proposed acquisitions will help meet identified affordable housing need within the borough and will form part of the housing stock transferring to West Surrey Council on 1 April 2027, thereby supporting the delivery of housing services by the successor authority.

findings.paper_title: Executive report - Affordable housing acquisitions in Farnham 150926
findings.headline: Independent viability appraisals confirm schemes fall within Council financial parameters; risks identified around rental income assumptions, maintenance costs, and shared ownership valuations.
findings.detail: Haverly Consulting independently reviewed business cases and viability assessments. Council identifies risks that assumptions (rental income, maintenance costs) may change, to be managed through New Development Impact Reserve. Right to Buy risk flagged: if tenants exercise this before borrowing repaid, retention calculations and Reserve provide protection. Shared ownership valuations to be updated before marketing homes.
findings.matters: HRA taking on long-term revenue exposure; early redemption risk from Right to Buy and valuation shortfall risk on shared ownership sales both affect scheme cash flows and debt servicing.
findings.figures: £14,454,118 budget; 8 shared ownership units at Waverley, 3 at Farnham Oaks create sales-dependent cash flows
findings.quote: There is a risk that some of the assumptions underpinning the business cases and accompanying viability appraisals, including rental income, management costs and maintenance costs, may change over time, adversely affecting the projected net revenue position.

findings.paper_title: Executive report - Affordable housing acquisitions in Farnham 150926
findings.headline: Acquisition subject to West Surrey Shadow Authority Executive consent under Section 24 Direction as capital contract exceeds £1m threshold.
findings.detail: As part of local government reorganisation, West Surrey councils must obtain written consent from shadow authority for contracts exceeding £1m. This acquisition falls outside scope of General Consents granted June 2026. Consent must be obtained before Executive and Council decisions take effect. Timeline: Executive 6 October, Full Council 10 November, then Shadow Executive approval required before completion.
findings.matters: Introduces procedural gate and potential delay risk to project execution during reorganisation period when successor authority must approve major financial commitments.
findings.quote: The recommendations in this report fall within the scope of the Section 24 Direction but not within the scope of the General Consent, and therefore the Executive and Council is taking the decision subject to the consent of the Shadow Executive being obtained.

findings.paper_title: Executive report - Affordable housing acquisitions in Farnham 150926
findings.headline: Council acquiring 48 affordable homes across two Farnham sites for £14.45m through combination of HRA borrowing and capital receipts.
findings.detail: Waverley Gardens (40 homes: 32 social rent, 8 shared ownership) and Farnham Oaks (8 homes: 5 affordable rent, 3 shared ownership). Acquisition supports Council's housing delivery programme and meets identified local housing need. Independent appraisals confirm financial viability; contingency allowances included in budget.
findings.matters: Large HRA capital investment decision; financing uses HRA borrowing flexibility available after government removed housing investment caps.
findings.figures: £14,454,118 total budget; 40 homes at Waverley Gardens, 8 homes at Farnham Oaks
findings.quote: The acquisitions will be funded through a combination of HRA borrowing and capital receipts, as detailed in Exempt Annex 2.

findings.headline: Service user receivables total £2.36m with 78% more than 90 days overdue, including £474.6k over one year old
findings.detail: Service user and fee payer receivables total £2,355,391. Of this, £1,830,821 is outstanding for more than 90 days, comprising £705,834 in the 90-180 day bracket, £650,372 in the 180-365 day bracket, and £474,615 aged over one year. The current amount (0-90 days) is £524,571.
findings.matters: The aging profile of receivables affects cash flow and liquidity; large overdue balances increase bad debt write-off risk and require provisioning, impacting available resources.
